queues.title: Rules
queues.text: Shall this rule settle what it fits, with no person reading each?
queues.rule: None is adopted until you say yes. Read what could go wrong and the items drawn at random. Yes settles each item it fits that you have not answered, and names the rule in its line. No changes nothing. Undo takes it back.

queues.title: Boroughs you know
queues.text: How well do you know this borough?
queues.rule: Go by the ground you have lived on, worked on or walked.

queues.title: Kinds of venue
queues.rule: Go by the name and the category as written. If they do not say, answer that you cannot tell.

flags.name_says_another_kind: its name says another kind of place
flags.one_of_many_records: the same name is on more than one record
flags.in_two_kinds: the record stands under two kinds

queues.title: Commons
queues.text: Is this place in the file, with a name and a way in?
queues.rule: Go by what the file holds. A way in is a gate or a path that the file marks.

answers.label: In the file, with a name and a way in
In the file, with no name or no way in

flags.no_match: nothing in the file has a name like it
flags.no_name: the nearest match has no name
flags.no_way_in: the nearest match has no way in

queues.title: Figures
queues.text: Does this figure look wrong for this area?
queues.rule: Your answer changes no figure. It makes the list to read before a release is approved.

flags.no_evidence: no record of evidence stands behind it
flags.moved_between_releases: it moved by a fifth or more since the release before
flags.far_from_neighbours: it is far above or far below every area beside it
flags.zero_thin_cover: it is zero, and the source covers only part of the area

queues.title: Sentences
queues.text: Is this sentence fit to quote about the place?
queues.rule: Choose the first fault that holds. If none holds, it is fit. Judge what it says, not whether it is true.

queues.title: Names
queues.text: Is this the name of an area?
queues.rule: Use what you know and what the page shows. Copy no name and no border from a map or a website. Move a border for the ground, never for who lives there. If you rely on a document, give its address in the note.

cells.short: This area has ground. To turn its name down waits for a new draft.
cells.words: The desk cannot take ground from an area. Turn this name down and the answer is saved, and set aside when a build's files are made. Read every name first. Then make the draft again from the answers. Then look at borders.
cells.saved: It is set aside until the draft is made again from the answers.

names.short: Other names are given to this area. To turn its name down waits on them.
names.words: An area goes only once no other name is given to it. Turn this name down and the answer is saved, and set aside while another name of the area is kept. Decide its other names first.
names.saved: It is set aside while another name is given to this area.

flags.one_publisher: one publisher writes this name, and one is not enough for it
flags.same_name_elsewhere: the same name stands in another place
flags.describes_residents: the name may say who lives there
flags.no_receipt: it rests on a file that has no receipt
flags.look_hard: the draft has a mark on it to settle

queues.title: Ratings
queues.rule: Rate the streets, buildings and places you know. Not the people who live there, and not what you have heard. The rubric says what 1 and 5 mean.

covers.label: I do not know this area

queues.title: Articles
queues.text: Is this the article about this place?
queues.rule: Go by the title and by what you know of the place. Open no page: the words of an article are read later, claim by claim.

answers.label: Yes, it is about this place

queues.title: Claims
queues.text: May this be shown as the source's words about this area?
queues.rule: Accept only if it is about this place, describes no people, passes no judgement, and a resident would find it fair.

answers.label: No. It is not about this place
No. A resident would not find it fair

flags.no_reference: the source gives no reference for it
